fresh_internal_checks.check: The statement fixes a connected compact complex manifold of dimension at least two and a Hermitian background; no bounded mass hypothesis is used.
The polar restriction is defined coefficientwise for the positive first curvature current, rather than as a nonlinear Monge-Ampere measure.
The existing isolated-logarithmic-pole cutoff lemma supplies a global witness for each sufficiently small coefficient.
The coefficient threshold is chosen strictly below the reciprocal curvature-loss bound, making the witness admissible.
Rational positive coefficients meet the manuscript analytic-singularity convention.
The existing analytic-envelope theorem gives an ordinarily equivalent normalized ordinary and ideal model.
Ordinary equivalence supplies the bounded local remainder at the pole and local boundedness everywhere else.
The pole set is exactly the designated point, so no other polar-current coefficient can contribute.
Different logarithmic coefficients have unbounded differences and hence different ordinary singularity classes.
The smooth-center ideal formula is applied in codimension n with the established logarithm and weight conventions.
The integer exponent max(floor(ta)-n+1,0) is valid also at its endpoint weights.
Distinct positive coefficients are distinguished at sufficiently large weights, without claiming a nontrivial ideal at every weight.
The positive trace measure uses the smooth closed local form beta=ddc|z|^2; its definition does not require omega closed.
Smooth cutoffs equal one on the smaller ball, vanish outside the larger ball and have two-sided Hessian bounds.
Their Hessian support lies in the annulus where the full bounded-remainder logarithmic estimate applies.
Distributional integration by parts is legitimate for the locally integrable potential and uses closedness only of beta.
The smooth background term is bounded by a constant times epsilon^(2n).
The annular Hessian integral is bounded by epsilon^(2n-2)(1+|log epsilon|) with a fixed coefficient-dependent constant.
Both bounds vanish in dimension at least two; the curve case is expressly excluded.
Positivity dominates all coefficient measures by the trace measure, so absence of a trace atom gives zero restriction to the singleton pole set.
The zero potential is an ordinary and ideal model for a Hermitian background and also has zero polar current.
The example rules out comparisons depending only on this fixed background and its first polar current; it does not close the general topology problem or assert novelty.
